name: NCS20072DR2G
title: Rail-to-rail output 3 MHz CMOS operational amplifiers, single, dual and quad, 2.7 V to 36 V
summary: CMOS operational amplifiers with a rail-to-rail output, 3 MHz of unity-gain bandwidth and a 2.8 V/µs slew rate, running from a single 2.7 V to 36 V supply at about 405 µA per channel. The PMOS input draws a few picoamps and its common mode range reaches from the negative rail to 1.35 V below the positive one. NCS20071, NCS20072 and NCS20074 are the single, dual and quad; the NCV versions are the AEC-Q100 automotive grade. NCS20072DR2G is the dual in SOIC-8.

operation.text: NCx20071 is the single (TSOP-5, SOT553-5), NCx20072 the dual (Micro8, SOIC-8, TSSOP-8) and NCx20074 the quad (SOIC-14, TSSOP-14). Each is a CMOS amplifier with a rail-to-rail output and 3 MHz of bandwidth, drawing 405 µA per channel typical at 2.7 V. NCV parts are the automotive grade: AEC-Q100 qualified, PPAP capable, with site and change control. All parts are Pb-free, halogen free and RoHS compliant.
The part runs from 2.7 V to 36 V on one supply, or ±1.35 V to ±18 V split, across −40 °C to 125 °C. The absolute limit across the supply pins is 40 V.

The common mode range runs from VSS up to VDD − 1.35 V, which is 16.65 V on ±18 V supplies. On ±18 V the offset of ten sample units stays flat to about 16.8 V of common mode voltage, then drops to about −14 mV by 17.2 V to 17.3 V. The absolute rating lets either input go 0.2 V beyond each rail. Input bias current is 5 pA typical at 25 °C and climbs steeply above about 85 °C, to about 1 nA at 125 °C (VS = 36 V).

The input pair is PMOS, with ESD diodes to both rails and a 1 kΩ resistor in each input lead. Two Zener diodes back to back, 5.5 V reverse voltage, join the two gates. Input current is limited to 10 mA. Above 26 V of differential input, external series resistance limits the current between the inputs: 500 Ω in series with each input holds it under 10 mA over the whole range up to 36 V.

The output stage is class AB with a rail-to-rail swing. With RL ≥ 10 kΩ the output comes within 5 mV to 74 mV typical of each rail, depending on supply; the distance from the rail grows in proportion to load current and rises with temperature. With the output shorted to a rail, the current it sources or sinks is the output current capability, 50 mA to 70 mA typical; the absolute limit is ±100 mA. High output current can raise the junction past its 150 °C limit; the junction temperature at a given dissipation follows from θJA of the package.

Phase margin is about 50° with 25 pF of load and falls to about 14° at 300 pF and beyond (VS = 5 V, RL = 10 kΩ). Gain margin is 14 dB. Open loop output impedance is a few ohms up to about 10 kHz and rises to roughly 400 Ω at 1 MHz.
